title: The Departing Residence: Why the Same Borrower Now Qualifies Differently at Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and FHA, and How an Income Agent Keeps Them Apart
summary: A borrower buying a new home while keeping or selling the old one carries a second housing payment, and how much of it counts in DTI depends on the investor. Fannie Mae's SEL-2026-08 moved its rental income rules to B3-3.8 and stopped accepting a lease for a departing residence. Freddie Mac still uses one. FHA ties rental income from a vacated home to a 100-mile relocation. A technical account of the three rules, the pending-sale exception, and how our agents compute qualifying income per investor.
body_markdown:
## Who This Is For


Underwriters, credit policy owners and secondary marketing teams at lenders who deliver to both GSEs and originate FHA, especially move-up purchase lenders where a large share of buyers already own a home. Also anyone who maintains income calculation logic and has not yet changed it for Fannie Mae's September 2026 Selling Guide update.


## The Second Housing Payment


A borrower buying a new principal residence while still owning the current one has two housing payments until the old home is sold or rented. The departing residence's full PITIA, principal, interest, taxes, insurance and any association dues, goes into the debt-to-income ratio unless a rule lets the lender exclude or offset it. On a move-up purchase that is often the difference between a 38% DTI and a 52% one, so the rules for excluding or offsetting that payment decide a large share of these loans.


There are two ways out. If the old home is being sold, the payment may come out entirely. If it is being kept and rented, projected rental income may offset it. The rules for both differ by investor, and one of them changed this autumn.


## Pending Sale: The Cleanest Exception


[Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-6-06](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-6-06/qualifying-impact-other-real-estate-owned) covers a current principal residence that is pending sale but will not close before the new loan. Fannie Mae does not require the current residence's PITIA in qualifying if the lender has the executed sales contract for the current residence and confirmation that any financing contingencies have been cleared.


Both documents have to be in the file, and the second is the one that goes missing. A signed contract with a buyer whose own financing contingency is still open is not a pending sale for this purpose. If the contingency has not cleared, the payment stays in DTI, the lender needs reserves to cover it, or the borrower needs to qualify some other way.


## Fannie Mae Now Uses Market Rent, Not the Lease


On September 2, 2026, Fannie Mae published[Announcement SEL-2026-08](https://singlefamily.fanniemae.com/media/document/pdf/announcement-sel-2026-08-selling-guide-updates) , which reorganized its rental income guidance into a new section, B3-3.8. The old general rental income topic, B3-3.1-08, became[B3-3.8-01](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-3.8-01/general-rental-income-information) , and the departing residence now has its own topic,[B3-3.8-05, Rental Income from Non-Subject Property: Departing Residence](https://selling-guide.fanniemae.com/sel/b3-3.8-05/rental-income-non-subject-property-departing-residence) .


The substantive change is that a lease agreement is no longer accepted to establish rental income on a departing residence. Gross rent comes from market rent, documented by the sources the topic accepts, such as a comparable rent schedule from an appraiser, and the lender must keep in the file all the documentation used to determine it. The lender must also document the borrower's current housing payment to use any rental income from the departing residence.


The calculation is to take 75% of gross monthly market rent and subtract the departing residence's PITIA. If the result is positive, it offsets that PITIA and nothing more. It cannot be added to qualifying income. If the result is negative, the shortfall goes into DTI as a debt. Industry summaries of the announcement also describe an added reserve requirement, six months of the departing residence's PITIA, where the borrower has less than 12 months of documented rental management experience.


On effective dates, investor bulletins have described the timing differently, some treating the changes as effective immediately and others tying the rental income revisions to applications dated on or after November 1, 2026. Check the announcement and your investor's bulletin before deciding which rule applies to a file in progress, because a file taken in October and underwritten in November can fall on either side.


Fannie Mae did not explain its reasoning at length, but a lease on a home the borrower has not yet moved out of is the easiest income document in mortgage lending to create. The tenant can be a relative, the rent can be set to whatever makes the ratio work, and nothing about the lease proves the house will rent for that amount. Market rent from an appraiser is harder to shape.


## Freddie Mac Still Takes the Lease


Freddie Mac's rental income rules in[Guide section 5306.1](https://guide.freddiemac.com/app/guide/section/5306.1) still work from a lease. The lease must be current and fully executed, and rental income is 75% of gross monthly rent from it, supported by evidence such as receipt of two months' rent, or the security deposit and first month's rent, or an appraisal with rental data. If no borrower has at least one year of investment property management experience, net rental income is limited to the amount that offsets the PITI. Freddie Mac's Bulletin 2024-9 relaxed that test from all borrowers to at least one.


## FHA Asks Why the Borrower Is Moving


FHA starts from a different question. Under the rental income policy in Handbook 4000.1, as updated by[Mortgagee Letter 2023-17](https://www.hud.gov/sites/dfiles/OCHCO/documents/2023-17hsgml.pdf) , rental income from a principal residence the borrower is vacating can be used only if the borrower is relocating to an area more than 100 miles from the current residence. Where there is no rental history on the property since the last tax filing, the lender needs an appraisal showing market rent, documented equity of at least 25%, and a lease of at least one year beginning after the new loan closes. A borrower moving across town to a bigger house carries the full PITIA on an FHA loan, however much the old house would rent for.


## One Borrower, Three Results


Take a borrower with $11,000 a month in gross income, buying a $640,000 home five miles away, with illustrative numbers throughout. The departing residence has a PITIA of $2,300 and a signed lease to a cousin at $3,000 a month, and an appraiser's comparable rent schedule puts market rent at $2,600. The new home's PITIA is $3,900, and other debts are $450. The borrower has never been a landlord.


Departing residence treatment Monthly debts in DTI DTI


Fannie Mae 75% of $2,600 market rent = $1,950, which is $350 short of the $2,300 PITIA, so the $350 shortfall counts as a debt. Six months of departing PITIA in reserves required. $3,900 + $450 + $350 = $4,700 42.7%


Freddie Mac 75% of the $3,000 lease = $2,250. With no management experience, it offsets PITI only, and $50 remains as a debt. $3,900 + $450 + $50 = $4,400 40.0%


FHA Not relocating more than 100 miles, so no rental income. Full $2,300 PITIA counts. $3,900 + $450 + $2,300 = $6,650 60.5%


Same borrower, same houses, and the result depends on where the loan is going. An income figure that does not say which investor's rules it was computed under is not an answer to "does this borrower qualify."


## How Our Income Agent Handles the Departing Residence


The[Income Desk](https://www.seiright.com/for-lenders/income-desk) computes qualifying income and the departing residence's effect on DTI under each investor's rules the lender delivers to, not just the one on the loan today. The rules are in the[Rulebook](https://www.seiright.com/how-it-works#rulebook) with their effective dates, so the pre-SEL-2026-08 Fannie Mae rule from B3-3.1-08 and the new B3-3.8-05 rule sit side by side, and the application date picks between them. Our post on[Rulebook change management](https://www.seiright.com/blog/rulebook-change-management-agency-selling-guide-updates-ai-mortgage-effective-dates) covers how a guide update becomes a dated rule rather than an overnight change to every file.


For each computation, the desk records which documents it used and why it ignored others. On a Fannie Mae file, a lease in the file is noted and not used for income. On a Freddie Mac file, it is used if it is current and executed and the rent receipts or deposit are there. On an FHA file, the desk first checks the distance between the two addresses and stops if it is under 100 miles. Each figure is cited to the page it came from, and each passes through[Triple Check](https://www.seiright.com/how-it-works#triple-check) .


A pending sale is checked for both documents. The[Document Concierge](https://www.seiright.com/for-lenders/document-concierge) requests the executed contract and the evidence that the buyer's financing contingency has cleared, and the[Conditions Manager](https://www.seiright.com/for-lenders/conditions-manager) keeps the departing PITIA in DTI until both are in the file. If the sale on the old house falls through after approval, the change in the[Loan Graph](https://www.seiright.com/platform/loan-graph) re-runs the calculation and reopens the file.


The lease to the cousin raises one more check. Our[Fraud Agent](https://www.seiright.com/for-lenders/fraud-agent) compares a departing-residence lease against market rent, the tenant's name against the borrowers and other parties to the file, and the stated occupancy plan against the insurance and any rental listing. A lease 15% above the appraiser's market rent to a tenant who shares the borrower's surname is not proof of anything. It goes to the underwriter as a review item with both documents.


## What Stays With the Underwriter


The desk does not choose the investor, which is a secondary marketing decision, and it does not decide whether a borrower with a 42.7% DTI and the required reserves should be approved. Where the program allows judgement, such as whether a borrower's prior experience managing a relative's rental counts as property management history, the question goes to the underwriter with the evidence. What the agent does is make sure the underwriter sees the departing residence computed three ways, with the reason each figure differs, before the loan is locked to one of them.
